'''Hunger''' is effectively removed in [[Matcha Flavoured]]. The hunger bar is hidden, the player's food level is never allowed to fall to where sprinting stops, and [[food]] is eaten for its healing and status effects rather than to fill a bar. The {{EffectLink|Hunger}} status effect instead stops the player from healing while it lasts.

== Mechanics ==
=== Food level ===
{{Diagram|Food level|width=360|align=right|caption=The food level the pack refills at 8 or below, so it never falls to vanilla's sprinting threshold.}}
Every tick, the pack checks each player's food level (0 to 20, where vanilla shows 2 points per drumstick). At 8 or below, the player is given {{MCW|Saturation}} II with a duration of 1, which refills it. Saturation is an instant effect, so the game reads that duration as 1 tick rather than 1 second: each time, the effect acts once and restores 2 food points, and it's given again on the next tick while the level is still 8 or below.<ref name="mh">{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/manage_hunger.mcfunction}}</ref>

The food level is therefore back at 9 or 10 within a tick of dropping to 8, well above 6, the vanilla threshold for sprinting, so the player can always sprint and never starves. After spawning or respawning, the food level starts at 20, as in vanilla; above the refill it drains as in vanilla and isn't lowered by the pack. The effect is hidden from the HUD.

=== Hunger bar ===
The resource pack replaces every food icon on the HUD with a blank texture, so the hunger bar isn't shown.<ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/textures/gui/sprites/hud/food_full.png}}</ref>

=== Eating ===
The pack's cooked foods have no vanilla food component at all: they are consumables that can always be eaten and restore no hunger (before 1.12.3 they had a food component with 0 nutrition and 0 saturation and the <code>can_always_eat</code> option). For example, [[bread]] instead grants {{EffectLink|Regeneration}} and removes harmful effects.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/food/oven/bread.json}}</ref> What a food does is described by its [[intrinsic]] and its tooltip. See [[Food]] and [[Cooking]].

Vanilla foods that still have a food component (from the Creative inventory, for example) restore food points as usual, and can't be eaten once the food level reaches 20.

=== Natural regeneration ===
{{Main|Natural regeneration}}
Natural regeneration is turned off with a game rule, so a high food level doesn't heal the player.

== Hunger effect ==
On Normal and Hard, the {{EffectLink|Hunger}} status effect stops the player from healing: whenever a player with Hunger has {{EffectLink|Regeneration}}, the Regeneration is removed, whether it was given before or after the Hunger.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/effects/regeneration/mark_player.mcfunction}}</ref> Since [[food]] heals through a hidden Regeneration effect, eating doesn't heal until the Hunger ends. On Easy, Hunger does nothing beyond its vanilla drain on the food level, which the pack refills (above).

While the effect lasts on Normal and Hard, the action bar shows a green timer that empties as the effect runs out, with a ticking sound every second once fewer than about 50 seconds remain; when the Hunger ends, the bar turns white and the experience orb pickup sound plays.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/effects/hunger/effect.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/effects/hunger/mark_player.mcfunction}}</ref>

Hunger is in the pack's list of harmful effects, so [[bread]], [[Honey Ginger Tea|honey ginger tea]] and [[ice cream]] remove it, and a [[milk bottle]] clears it with every other effect.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/tags/mob_effect/harmful.json}}</ref> [[Husk]]s inflict it with their hits, as in vanilla, and some foods and items apply it as a side effect:

{{Data/Effect/Hunger}}

== History ==
{{History|
{{History line|0.4-alpha|Removed the "You cannot eat right now" warning.}}
{{History line|1.12.3|The pack refills the food level at 7 or below instead of 6 or below, so it now rests at 8 or 9 instead of 7 or 8. Crafted and cooked foods lose their food component (which had 0 nutrition and 0 saturation) and are plain consumables.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/food/oven/bread.json}}</ref>}}
{{History line|1.12.6-alpha|The pack no longer gives Hunger to drain the food level at 10 or above, and it refills the food level at 8 or below instead of 7 or below. On Normal and Hard, the Hunger effect now removes Regeneration, so it stops healing, and shows a timer in the action bar. Bread and other foods that remove harmful effects now remove Hunger too.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/effects/regeneration/mark_player.mcfunction}}</ref>}}
}}

== Trivia ==
* The developer found vanilla hunger "isn't very fun or engaging": "The punishment is not severe enough to be interesting and the remedy is not difficult enough to be engaging." They preferred the old Beta hunger system, where food healed directly.<ref>{{Cite video|quote=The sprinting limitation is good in theory, but in practice only serves to frustrate me. The punishment is not severe enough to be interesting and the remedy is not difficult enough to be engaging.}}</ref>
* The developer addressed the worry that unlimited sprinting makes mobs harmless by making [[Zombie|zombies]] much faster.<ref>{{Cite video|quote=If you can always sprint, doesn't that mean hostile mobs won't be a threat? But, put a pin in that. We'll come back to it later.}}</ref>
